newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Sierra Leone rebel chief mute on joining coup govt.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel chief mute on joining coup govt.

text.p: Sierra Leonean rebel leader Foday Sankoh on Monday declined to comment on an invitation from soldiers who seized power in the West African nation to join their government.
"You have to watch the situation before you talk," Sankoh said from the Nigerian capital Abuja where he has been kept by Nigeria's military rulers for the past two months.
He said on Sunday that he was not surprised by the coup that toppled President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Sankoh heads the Revolutionary United Front (RUF) which fought Sierra Leone troops in a civil war that began in 1991.
He reached an agreement with Kabbah's government last November to end the war that killed 10,000 people but skirmishes have persisted.

He denies he is being detained by Nigeria and says his mission here is to see military ruler General Sani Abacha to seek his contribution, as chairman of the Economic Community of West African States, to the Sierra Leone peace process.
"I have come here on a mission and I have to exercise patience," Sankoh said on Monday.
So far he has not seen Abacha or any senior Nigerian government official although he said he expected to meet Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi this week.

Nigeria has made no comment on his stay in the country nor has it said anything on the latest coup in Sierra Leone, where according to witnesses the soldiers who toppled Kabbah exchanged sustained fire with Nigerian troops stationed in the country.
